title: JudgmentRecordV5
description: A reasoned assessment with no external comparison behind it — paraphrase entailment, scope narrowing, tone, and the other questions a deterministic check cannot decide — recorded as a typed, replaceable artifact with named inputs, a named producer and a hashed question. NO JUDGMENT PROVIDER SHIPS IN v5.0. Nothing in this repository executes a judgment, no adapter is included, and `wi anchor` lists paraphrase entailment in `checks_not_run` rather than approximating it. This schema exists now so that the first implementation to arrive does not get to define the terms. A judgment provider is third-party infrastructure in this architecture, exactly like a PDF decoder or a hash function: named so it can be replaced, audited and disagreed with — never an author, never a contributor, never a signer, and no field here is one it could become one in. A provider has no write path into the graph; a judgment enters a workspace the way a supplied source does, as data examined before it is trusted. The `.wiab` bundle reserves `proof/judgments.jsonl` for these records and `build_bundle()` writes it empty.

judgment_id.description: Addressable identity of the record. A judgment nobody can point at cannot be contested, re-run or withdrawn.

kind.description: Which typed question was asked, for example `entailment`. A record without it cannot be re-run by a different provider or compared against the first. A provider is never sent a `kind` it did not declare in its capabilities.

input_hashes.description: Exactly what the provider saw, by role and by digest. Without this the judgment is unreproducible and its currency is undecidable — there would be no way to tell whether it is still about the text it was about.

role.description: What this input was to the question, for example `claim`, `anchor`, `source_state`.

node.description: Logical id of the node the input came from, when it came from one.

digest.description: Digest of the exact state supplied.

result.description: The verdict and a statement in words. NEVER A SCORE. A model's internal probabilities are real quantities a provider may keep in its own diagnostics and may use for routing — whether to escalate, whether to ask a second provider, whether to flag for human review — but they are never surfaced as evidence and never appear in a rendered proof line.

verdict.description: The named outcome of the typed question, for example `supports_with_scope_narrowing`.

statement.description: The reasoning in plain words, addressed to the person who has to decide what to do about it.

recommended_repair.description: A named repair route, for example `qualify_claim`. Advisory; it is never applied without a decision.

basis.description: Always the literal string `judged`, and there is no other legal value for this field. `verified` names how a result was produced — a deterministic comparison that actually executed — not how sure anybody is, so no confidence threshold and no provider quality promotes a judgment into a verification. A provider that emits `verified` is rejected at the schema boundary as a hard error rather than coerced to the correct value, because a provider that tried is a provider with a defect worth seeing.

provider.description: Who ran it. An unnamed provider cannot be audited, compared or replaced, so identity is mandatory rather than courteous.

provider_id.description: Stable identity of the provider implementation.

adapter_version.description: Version of the adapter that translated between the core and the provider. It translates only; it has no handle on the workspace.

model.description: What it ran on. 'A language model' is not an identifier. This block names third-party infrastructure and nothing else; it is not an authorship field and confers no credit.

identifier.description: Identifier of the inference engine used.

version.description: Version of that engine. A different version is a different producer and a re-run under it is a new judgment.

policy_hash.description: Digest of the decision policy in force when the judgment was requested. Under what rules the answer was interpreted.

prompt_template_hash.description: Digest of the question template the provider was given. A judgment whose question is unknown is unreviewable — a reader cannot tell whether the answer is to the question they care about.

created_at.description: When the judgment was recorded. Judgments age; this is what lets a policy expire them on time as well as on state.

expires_if.description: The dependency contract, carried in the record itself. A judgment is not a permanent fact about two texts; it is a fact about two STATES under one policy. Change the claim, the anchor or the policy and the record does not silently continue to apply — it is marked stale and either re-run or shown as expired. This is what wires a judgment into the staleness system.

digest.description: A SHA-256 digest in the canonical `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` form.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 instant with an explicit UTC offset.
